extracted.intended_audience: researchers, social-media analysts, and meme creators studying humor and virality in internet memes
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative rubric and descriptive criteria for what makes internet memes funny and likely to spread, covering humor types, virality factors, structural elements, format templates, and contemporary trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sarcasm
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as the most prevalent humor type in memes; typically depends on tone and implied meaning opposite to the literal text, often requiring shared cultural cues for recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silliness
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple, absurd, or playful content without deep setup; common meme humor type that trades on low-stakes incongruity and immediate amusement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-defeating humor
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humor that targets the creator or in-group (self-deprecation) noted as particularly effective at promoting sharing and virality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humor based on comparing two states/people/ideas (often via juxtaposition or template formats) to highlight absurd differences or priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personification
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigning human attributes to objects/animals/concepts; used to create relatable or absurd scenarios in a compact meme format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exaggeration
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overstating characteristics or reactions to amplify comedic effect; common in image choices and captions to heighten incongruity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pun
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wordplay relying on multiple meanings or sound-alike words; can be effective but often culturally or language-dependent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprise
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humor that depends on an unexpected twist or reversal; in memes this often appears as an image-text mismatch or sudden punchline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humor (as virality factor)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fundamental driver of sharing — memes must elicit an amusement response to motivate forwarding, commenting, or remixing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intertextuality
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combining or referencing other texts/templates/cultural artifacts increases resonance for audiences who recognize the references and can reward cultural fluency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Juxtaposition
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placing elements that normally don't belong together to create conflict or surprise; central to many meme jokes (image vs caption or two-panel contrasts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cute / emotionally arousing content
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content that evokes positive affect or strong emotions can increase shareability independent of complex humor strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dopamine-triggering laughter
rubrics_metrics.description: Dopamine-triggering — laughter that neurologically rewards sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper notes that dopamine-driven pleasure from laughter contributes to why users share memes; implies designing for immediate, pleasurable reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimodality / image-text relationship
rubrics_metrics.description: Multimodal — Image + superimposed text; the image-text relationship IS the joke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Memes rely on the interaction between visual and textual elements; the joke often emerges from the relation rather than either modality alone. Multiple layers of meaning and advanced inferential strategies may be required for full appreciation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context-dependence / insider fluency
rubrics_metrics.description: Context-Dependence — rewards fast recognition + cultural fluency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Memes often rely on shared cultural knowledge; outsiders may miss the joke while insiders recognize it instantly. This inside-joke effect amplifies sharing within in-groups but can limit broader reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format templates
rubrics_metrics.description: Format Templates — recognizable templates carry pre-loaded meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using established templates (e.g., Distracted Boyfriend, Drake, Two Buttons, Galaxy Brain) leverages pre-existing associations and shortcuts interpretation, enabling rapid comprehension and remixing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absurdist / surreal trend
rubrics_metrics.description: Absurdist / surreal — lack setup-punchline; randomness itself is funny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contemporary trend where randomness and lack of traditional structure are the source of humor; may favor novelty and unpredictability over clear semantic jokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layered irony
rubrics_metrics.description: Layered irony — ironic memes about ironic memes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meta-irony increases complexity and can engage audiences who appreciate reflexive or self-referential humor; may require higher cultural fluency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gen Z humor / post-ironic
rubrics_metrics.description: Gen Z humor — deliberately incoherent, post-ironic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A style characterized by intentional incoherence and post-irony; often resists clear reading and privileges in-group recognition and novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format mutation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful meme templates change rapidly; staying current requires awareness of template evolution and creative adaptation to new variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognizable format/template (rubric item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does it use a recognizable format/template?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit rubric item: using a known template helps instant recognition and leverages pre-loaded meanings; absence of a template may require stronger alternative cues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image-text incongruity (rubric item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the image-text combination create incongruity?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit rubric item: the joke should emerge from a tension or mismatch between the visual and textual elements; this incongruity is a primary source of humor in memes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural reference / intertextuality (rubric item)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit rubric item: presence of recognizable cultural references increases resonance for audiences who share that knowledge and can heighten humor via association.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rewards in-group fluency (rubric item)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit rubric item: memes that favor insiders (fast recognition and shared knowledge) tend to be amplified within communities; consider trade-off between niche virality and broad appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shareability / immediate readability (rubric item)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit rubric item: memes should be compact and quickly interpretable to maximize likelihood of being reshared; visual clarity, succinct text, and immediate punchlines help.
